# 04 — Revision-bound requester approval

## Outcome

Make the generated plan revision content-addressed and executable only after
the requester approves that exact revision; a semantic replan invalidates the
approval and requires a new review/approval.

## Non-goal

Do not treat a self-declared actor, test pass, readiness result, or generic
reaction as requester authority, and do not execute work.

## Inputs and implementation boundary

Use W3 plan generation and the existing Mission output-history evidence as a
starting constraint. Persist an approval decision bound to mission id,
revision, digest, decision authority, and timestamp.

Use the requester-decision adapter defined in the
[design notes](ARTIFACTS.md#settled-design-notes-proposals-not-current-apis).
Do not reinterpret the existing synthetic/generic reaction event as an
execution grant. Unknown authority fails closed, with no executable plan.
All activation/dispatch/resume entry points consume the same approval check;
a convenient named MCP operation must not bypass the underlying domain gate.

Plan preparation runs both cold walkthrough and distinct formal review on
the current revision before presenting it for requester approval. A semantic
change invalidates those verdicts and the grant. Read-only regeneration and
progress/evidence recording do not themselves edit the approved plan.

## Expected post-state and validation

The approval gate rejects execution before approval and after a semantic
change; it accepts only a matching requester decision. A nonsemantic
read/render does not invalidate approval. Restart replay preserves the
decision/digest association.

Future target: `cd workflow-tools && cargo test -p mission`; include approve,
stale approval, replan/reapprove, and restart cases.

## Checkpoint

Commit approval model and regression tests after passing.
